Six more endpoint groups, a rate limiter that no longer spends your request timeout, and a guard on the public surface. **90 of IBKR's 108 Trading endpoints.**

## What is new

| Group | Endpoints | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Watchlists | 4 | create, read, list, delete |
| Scanner | 2 | the parameter reference and a scan |
| FYIs and Notifications | 11 | settings, disclaimers, delivery options, notifications |
| Event Contracts | 5 | the category tree down to a contract's schedule |
| Alerts | 5 | listing, details, the MTA alert, activation, deletion |
| PortfolioAnalyst | 4 | performance, all periods, allocation, transactions |

That is 31 endpoints, all modelled after probing a live gateway rather than from the reference alone. `Execution` and the four trade-time encodings, which `v0.1.0` shipped without live coverage, now have it.

## Fixed: the rate limiter was spending your request timeout

Pacing ran in a `DelegatingHandler`, and `HttpClient.Timeout` covers the whole handler chain — so a request held back to respect an IBKR limit spent that time out of the budget for the call it was about to make. Both defaults are thirty seconds, which makes the longest wait `MaxWait` permits exactly the whole timeout. Seven quick calls to `/portfolio/accounts` at one per five seconds put the last at a thirty-second wait, and it failed as

```
IbkrApiException: GET /v1/api/portfolio/accounts timed out.
```

for a request that had never been sent. Pacing now happens in `IbkrApiClient`, before `HttpClient` starts its clock. Nothing changes about what is paced; the timeout goes back to measuring only what IBKR is responsible for.

## What probing found this time

**A `200 OK` that means "not found".** `GET /iserver/account/alert/{alertId}` answers an unknown alert with a success status and `{"error": "Alert with order ID=... not found."}`. Deserialized naively that is an alert with no name, no account and no conditions. `GetDetailsAsync` reads the body and throws.

**A response that hides its data under your account number.** `POST /pa/allperiods` documents seven fields, none of which is the performance. The figures arrive under a property named after the account, and inside it the period names are themselves property names. A model bound to the documented schema deserializes cleanly and returns nothing — the worst way for this to fail — so it is read by a converter instead.

**Requests IBKR's own reference calls valid and its gateway rejects.** `POST /pa/transactions` documents `acctIds`, `conids` and `currency` as optional and offers `{}` as its example. A live gateway answers `400 Bad Request: acctIds, currency and conids are required`. At one request per fifteen minutes, that is a quarter of an hour to discover. The client fills in IBKR's own documented default and refuses a missing account before sending.

**An enum whose documented values the endpoint rejects.** IBKR's two descriptions of `/pa/performance`'s `period` disagree. The reference offers `3M`, `6M` and `12M`; the gateway answers `400 Bad Request: Invalid period: 3M`. `PerformancePeriod` carries the six that actually work.

**A type code list that is not the list IBKR sends.** `/fyi/settings` publishes twenty-three codes as a closed enum and returns thirty, eleven of them on no list anywhere — one of which appears in IBKR's own example response. `NotificationTypeCode` is an open struct, because an enum would turn every unlisted code into a failure of the whole response.

**A tenth and an eleventh time format.** Event contracts send a twelve-hour clock (`4:15 PM`) in the zone `US/Central`, a TZDB backward link rather than the canonical `America/Chicago`. PortfolioAnalyst sends `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss` with no stated zone; two calls timed from a host an hour ahead of UTC established that it is UTC, and the live sweep re-checks that on every run.

## Breaking changes

Seven request records are now `internal`: `ContractRulesRequest`, `OrderReplyRequest`, `OrderSubmissionRequest`, `SuppressMessagesRequest`, `ScannerRequest`, `InitializeBrokerageSessionRequest` and `CreateWatchlistRequest`. They are wire shapes the clients build for themselves — no public member accepted or returned any of them, so nothing could be passed one. They were found by transcribing the public surface for the first time.

## New: the public surface is now pinned

Both packages carry a transcript of their public API under `tests/*/PublicApi/`, checked on every test run. A deliberate change updates the file in the commit that makes it; an accidental one fails the build and names the lines.

## Verified live

`samples/IbkrDotNet.Samples.Verify` sweeps every implemented endpoint against a running gateway. Of the 90, all but ten have been exercised there. The ten are the seven notification writes — they change settings on the username and IBKR publishes no way to read a value before overwriting it — and the three alert endpoints that need an alert to already exist, which no IBKR endpoint can create.

## Not in this release

WebSocket streaming is out of scope. The remaining 18 endpoints are the two Financial Advisor groups, tracked as [#21](https://github.com/jerbersoft/ibkrdotnet/issues/21) and [#22](https://github.com/jerbersoft/ibkrdotnet/issues/22). `IIbkrApiClient` reaches them today with authentication, rate limiting and error mapping intact.

Attached to this release. Nothing is published to NuGet yet.
